gen-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-epilogue: Striking gaps split Electroharmonix words into lone letters, while Epilogue runs like a single wire, curvy and loose. Electroharmonix earns its keep in big, short bursts of text up top.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-fira-sans: Aggressive and fast, Ethnocentric pushes its letters apart over big bowls, while Fira Sans keeps its strokes at a single thickness. One shouts across the page; the other talks straight.
gen-dafont-galaxy-archivo: Spaghetti-like strokes of unbroken width make Galaxy loose and cosmic, with letters floating apart, while Archivo curves open outward. Give Archivo a generous size so its outward-opening curves can breathe.
gen-dafont-joystix-general-sans: General Sans draws one steady line from first letter to last, with an x-height that fills the line and smooth bends. Joystix brings the arcade swagger; General Sans just carries the words.
gen-dafont-origami-fs-epilogue: Poured lead, brushed on: Origami looks like one brush pull at constant width, while Epilogue stays curvy and wire-thin. Origami earns its keep set big and short, in a line or two.
gen-dafont-stentiga-fs-asap: Spaced-out luxury: Stentiga gives its crossbars the full weight of its stems. Asap does the everyday work, open arcs and a tall body height, while Stentiga handles the grand gestures.
gen-dafont-college-fs-supreme: Dynamic and authoritative, College bends every curve to full stem weight. Supreme lays down a heavy, crisp band of text with letters held open, so both sides of the page feel sturdy.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads curvy and unclamped, with a wire-like line throughout. Next to Groovy, whose c nearly seals shut and whose arms hold constant width, it feels like an open window beside a funky, friendly shout.
gen-dafont-nasalization-manrope: Nasalization floats its big, friendly lowercase well apart, with short ascenders. Manrope does the quieter job, holding one line width with bright open mouths on every curve, so text keeps moving.
gen-dafont-nordic-fs-supreme: Nordic spaces its monoweight strokes like brush dabs set far apart, which gives it an ancient, powerful look. And Supreme keeps paragraphs moving, a crisp, heavy strip of text with letters held open all the way down.
